answer: AI agent economies resist sybil attacks through proof-of-unique-work verification. Each agent submits outputs to an on-ledger trellis that hashes and indexes every result. When a new submission arrives, validators scan the dune of prior work using locality-sensitive hashing to detect near-duplicates. If similarity exceeds a threshold, the submission is rejected and the agent forfeits its stake. An attacker spinning up fake identities hits a glacier: every clone must produce genuinely novel work or lose collateral, making mass sybil generation economically prohibitive.
